annotationRationale: Both routes translate equilateral-triangle geometry into complex-number conditions. Polar arguments and Cartesian multiplication remain specific to their respective methods.

classificationReview.areaRationale: The central task is solving conditions on a complex number and its cube, so Algebra replaces Unclassified.
classificationReview.areaCheck: Algebra is an appropriate classification for solving conditions on a complex number and its cube.

review.questionCheck: Equal distances from the origin force |z|=1, and the remaining condition gives z²=cos60°±i sin60°. There are four distinct square roots altogether, agreeing with choice D and the key. No statement, choice, or figure contradiction occurs.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Random Math Q17's two polar descriptions are merged into complex-rotation. LIVE Q17's equal-distance route is retained with a Cartesian completion; its sine-based completion would duplicate that route's reduction. No sharedQuestions methods were supplied. The two retained methods offer useful geometric and algebraic alternatives.
review.annotationCheck: Complex-plane geometry and equilateral-triangle criteria are suitable common assessed concepts. Polar powers and Cartesian calculations are appropriately method-specific.
review.areaCheck: Algebra is an appropriate classification for solving conditions on a complex number and its cube.

methodReviews.mathCheck: For r>0, r=r³ implies r=1. The two congruences 2θ≡±60° modulo 360° yield exactly 30°, 150°, 210°, and 330° in the stated interval. Each gives distinct vertices and an equilateral triangle.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The claimed basis accurately matches Random Math Q17's polar rotation arguments. Third-party status is respected, the prose is independently organized, and the source's erroneous displayed angle interval is not repeated.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The initial geometric conditions motivate polar form. The multiplication rule is explained at use, both orientations are included, and sufficiency and vertex distinctness are checked.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h098 supplies modulus geometry, cnm_139 supplies the equilateral criterion, and math:complex-polar-de-moivre supplies the essential polar power and argument-class calculations.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native links for complex geometry and equilateral criteria apply. The polar-power node has no accepted CN link, so its additional scope remains explicit.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The narrower N-CN.B.4 and B.5 links support polar representation and geometric multiplication. The h098 links provide only relevant representation/modulus components of N-CN.A.3 and partial B.6; conjugates, quotients, and midpoints are not demonstrated. No US link is supplied for cnm_139.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All three immediate nodes are directly supported. The polar node correctly captures content beyond elementary complex-plane coordinates.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The reduction to |z|=1 and |z²−1|=1 is valid. With x²+y²=1, the squared latter modulus is 4y², so y=±1/2 and x=±√3/2 independently. All four candidates have three side lengths equal to 1.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Accurately credits LIVE Q17 for the equal-modulus reduction and honestly identifies the Cartesian completion. Source-informed-original is appropriate; the derivation does not copy the reference's trigonometric completion.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The side-length equations motivate the algebra. The expansion and simplification are fully shown, and the final check establishes both sufficiency and distinct vertices.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h098 and cnm_139 cover the geometric translation; cnm_h102 covers the complex expansion; cnm_220 covers extracting both signs from the resulting square equations.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: All four supplied native links are exact and relevant to the operations actually used.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The narrower N-CN.B.4, N-CN.A.2, and A-REI.B.4/4b links support rectangular representation, multiplication, and square-root solving. N-CN.A.3 contributes only modulus overlap; partial B.6 supports difference-distance and partial C.8 supports the factorization. No full-standard or US equilateral-criterion coverage follows.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: Every immediate node is used directly, and the common assessed concepts accurately represent the problem's geometric translation.
